title: Plan screen: cadence bucket tabs, suggested qty, snooze/skip/exclude/override with revert-to-auto
goal: Build F11's centerpiece screen -- one tab per cadence bucket (daily...unpredictable), each listing items due in that bucket with a pack-size-aware suggested quantity, and four per-item manual actions (snooze, skip once, always exclude, move to a different cadence bucket) where the cadence-bucket override wins permanently over the nightly-recomputed value until explicitly reverted (A9). This directly consumes E-5's item_stats (cadence_bucket, cadence_override, confidence, predicted_next_purchase_at, daily_rate_base, interval_est_days) and reuses E-7's getInventoryItems() as its base data source, the same way S-20 reused it for getItemsNeedingAttention().
in_scope: lib/plan/data.ts (server-only): getPlanItems() -> PlanItem[] built on top of getInventoryItems() (lib/inventory/data.ts), filtered to items with a non-null cadenceBucket (i.e. lastPurchasedAt !== null -- nothing to plan for an item with zero purchase history, matching computeItemStats's own null-cadence-bucket condition). Per item: effectiveCadenceBucket = item_stats.cadence_override ?? item_stats.cadence_bucket (item_stats.cadence_override is read here for the first time in the codebase -- it has existed unused in the schema and in recompute.ts's deliberate exclusion from the upsert payload since E-2/E-5 specifically so a later epic could add this read side; this story is that later epic). suggestedQtyBase computed per F11's formula: cycleConsumptionBase = dailyRateBase !== null ? dailyRateBase * intervalEstDays : null; if cycleConsumptionBase is null (no rate signal yet), suggestedQtyBase = defaultPackSize ?? 1 (a sane 'buy one pack' default, not a fabricated consumption number); else if defaultPackSize > 0, suggestedQtyBase = defaultPackSize * max(1, ceil(cycleConsumptionBase / defaultPackSize)); else (no pack size known) suggestedQtyBase = max(1, ceil(cycleConsumptionBase)) in base units, no pack rounding possible. dueDate = predictedNextPurchaseAt (already computed by E-5, unaffected by the bucket-label override -- overriding cadence_bucket only relabels which tab an item is browsed under, per working spec Sec5/F11; it is not a re-anchoring of the actual prediction date, and recompute.ts already never reads cadence_override for any computation, only excludes it from being clobbered).

Manual action state (snooze / skip once / always exclude) persisted in the existing, currently-unused `plan_entries` table (schema since E-2's full_schema migration: household_id, catalog_item_id, cadence_bucket, suggested_qty_base, due_date, state, snoozed_until). No schema migration needed -- this story is read-light: at most one row per (household_id, catalog_item_id) exists only once a manual action has ever been taken on that item; items with no plan_entries row are implicitly 'pending'. Row identity is resolved by an explicit select-then-insert-or-update in lib/plan/actions.ts (no DB unique constraint added, since writes are always exactly one row per single user action, never a bulk upsert) -- deliberately NOT the item_stats/cadence_override upsert-preserving-columns idiom, because this table's writes need to be conditional (see skip/snooze auto-expiry below), not a blind preserve-by-omission.

lib/plan/actions.ts ('use server'): setCadenceOverrideAction(catalogItemId, bucket | null) writes item_stats.cadence_override directly (null = revert to auto). snoozeItemAction(catalogItemId, days: 3|7|14) writes plan_entries {state:'snoozed', snoozed_until: now+days}. unsnoozeItemAction(catalogItemId) sets state back to 'pending', snoozed_until null. skipOnceAction(catalogItemId) writes {state:'skipped', due_date: <the item's CURRENT computed dueDate at the moment of the action, read fresh from getPlanItems()>} -- due_date here is the auto-expiry anchor, not a display cache. undoSkipAction(catalogItemId) sets state back to 'pending'. excludeItemAction(catalogItemId) writes {state:'excluded'}. includeItemAction(catalogItemId) sets state back to 'pending', snoozed_until null. Every action revalidatePath('/plan'), revalidatePath('/'), revalidatePath('/inventory').

getPlanItems() read-side auto-expiry (no write-back required for correctness, so no cron/regeneration job is needed): a plan_entries row with state='snoozed' is treated as 'pending' once snoozed_until <= now; state='skipped' is treated as 'pending' once the item's freshly-computed dueDate no longer equals the due_date stamped at skip time (i.e. a new cadence cycle has started -- the skip only ever suppresses the one occurrence it was taken against); state='excluded' never auto-expires, only includeItemAction() clears it.

app/plan/page.tsx: server component, one tab per CADENCE_ORDER bucket + 'unpredictable' (reuse lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts's exported CADENCE_ORDER/_internal, or lib/inventory/format.ts's CADENCE_LABELS for tab labels), selected via ?bucket= searchParam (defaults to the first bucket in order that has >=1 active -- not excluded, not currently-snoozed/skipped -- item; falls back to the first bucket with ANY item, then to 'daily' if the household has zero planned items at all). Per bucket: item count and a plain item list (no monetary running-total -- see design deviation below), each row showing suggested qty (via lib/inventory/format.ts's formatBaseQty), due date, and the four action controls (snooze duration picker, skip once, exclude, a cadence-bucket <select> that calls setCadenceOverrideAction, with a 'Revert to auto' button shown only when cadence_override is currently set). Snoozed/skipped/excluded items are visually set apart (not hidden) within their bucket with an undo/include-again control, since a user landing on a bucket should be able to see and reverse what they suppressed.

Design deviation from F11's literal text, stated explicitly rather than silently dropped: F11 mentions a per-bucket running cost total ('~₹2,340'). price_history.unit_price is persisted from receipt_lines.unit_price, which is priced per the ORIGINAL DISPLAY unit (e.g. per kg, per piece, per dozen) -- that display-unit basis is never stored alongside price_history, only the raw number. suggestedQtyBase is in BASE units (grams/ml/pieces). There is no safe, general conversion from one to the other for arbitrary items (a kg-priced item's per-gram cost is unit_price/1000; a piece-priced item's is unit_price/1; price_history alone cannot tell which). Computing a total anyway would silently produce numbers wrong by up to 3 orders of magnitude for weight/volume items -- worse than not showing a number. Scoped out of this story; a correct version needs either storing the display-unit basis alongside price_history or a documented per-item price-per-base-unit column, which belongs to F13 (Budget & insights, a later epic), not a silent guess here.
out_of_scope: Any change to computeItemStats.ts, recompute.ts, or the nightly cadence_bucket computation itself -- this story only ADDS a read of the already-existing, already-excluded-from-recompute cadence_override column plus a new write path for it. A9 is satisfied structurally: recompute.ts's toRow() has excluded cadence_override from its upsert payload since E-5, so a nightly recompute physically cannot touch it.
The Today view (due within 3 days across all buckets, default landing screen) -- E-8's S-22, which depends on this story's getPlanItems().
F12 shopping list generation, F13 budget/cost totals, F14 notifications -- later epics.

A DB-side cron/regeneration job that bulk-writes plan_entries.cadence_bucket / suggested_qty_base / due_date columns -- deliberately not built; those three columns are left unused/null except due_date, which is written only as the skip-expiry anchor on skipOnceAction. Everything else is computed live on each page load from item_stats + catalog_items, matching this repo's existing force-dynamic / no-persisted-cache convention (getInventoryItems, getItemsNeedingAttention).
acceptance: Manual cadence override survives nightly recompute; revert-to-auto restores computed value (A9).
invariants: setCadenceOverrideAction never writes to any column recompute.ts also writes -- it touches only item_stats.cadence_override, a column recompute.ts's toRow() has excluded by construction since E-5.

plan_entries writes never touch cadence_bucket or suggested_qty_base (those columns are left null by this story -- they are display-derived live, not persisted, so there is no stale-cache risk to reconcile).
getPlanItems() only includes items with a non-null cadenceBucket (>=1 purchase ever) -- an item with zero purchase history has no predictedNextPurchaseAt to plan against and must not appear.
A skip only suppresses the one due-occurrence it was taken against; it must not silently suppress the item forever once a new cadence cycle produces a later dueDate.
